evidence: Item 2, "UAE federal report cites agentic AI project and new AI authority", treats an 11 Oct 2026 year-in-review report [W10] as the event. The events it describes are not dated inside 05–11 Oct 2026. The brief admits "announcement date and powers are not given". The Federal Authority was already on the Week 40 watchlist, so it was announced before this week. The National Committee approval is undated [W10.2, W10.3]. evidence:
Workflow-excluded sources are disclosed as "none" (DC05 PASS). There is no personal data (DC06), and officials are named as reported in W01, W02 and W08. Failing instances are legal statements that do not come from the pack:
(1) Item 4 Why: "UK law applies to us only if we handle UK personal data." This is a definitive rule on UK data protection reach. W06 says nothing about territorial scope.
(2) Item 1 Why: "Direct EU AI Act duties on us depend on our placing nothing on the EU market." No pack extract states this.
(3) Item 3 Why: "so no duty on us follows." This is a legal conclusion about the Dubai frameworks, which W08 does not support.
why_it_matters: These sentences give readers legal conclusions that the pack does not support and that Legal has not checked. Two of them would wrongly reassure leadership that UK and EU rules do not reach us.
required_fix: Remove or soften the three legal conclusions to questions, e.g. "Whether UK data protection law reaches us is unconfirmed (Inference); check with Legal." Do the same for the EU and Dubai sentences.
